about_blocks.text: Field Trip Health Montreal is an outpatient clinic that offers ketamine-assisted psychotherapy. It is on the second floor of 397 Avenue Laurier Ouest, above the Mikado restaurant, in the Plateau-Mont-Royal area close to Mile End and Outremont. Appointments run Monday to Friday, 9am to 7pm, and you go home after each visit.

It is on the second floor of 397 Avenue Laurier Ouest, above the Mikado restaurant, in the Plateau-Mont-Royal area close to Mile End and Outremont. Appointments run Monday to Friday, 9am to 7pm, and you go home after each visit.

about_blocks.text: Most people who come here have depression, anxiety, PTSD, OCD, chronic pain or a substance use problem and have already tried medication or talk therapy without enough relief. The clinic's therapists also see clients for grief, ADHD, bipolar disorder, eating disorders, postpartum depression and complex trauma, and the team says it works with many veterans, first responders, healthcare workers and Indigenous clients. Staff speak English and French.

about_blocks.text: Getting started takes a few steps. You book a free 15-minute discovery call, fill in a questionnaire, then have a paid medical consultation with a nurse practitioner, who checks your health history and medications and decides whether ketamine is safe for you. The clinic's 2026 Montreal guide lists that consultation at $250 and notes that RAMQ does not cover it.

You book a free 15-minute discovery call, fill in a questionnaire, then have a paid medical consultation with a nurse practitioner, who checks your health history and medications and decides whether ketamine is safe for you. The clinic's 2026 Montreal guide lists that consultation at $250 and notes that RAMQ does not cover it.

about_blocks.text: If you are approved, a therapist meets you for a preparation session. Each dosing session lasts a little over two hours: a nurse gives a low dose of ketamine, usually as an intramuscular injection, while you rest in a zero-gravity chair with a weighted blanket and headphones, and your therapist stays in the room the whole time. Integration therapy afterwards helps you make sense of what came up. The standard programs have 6 or 9 dosing sessions.

about_blocks.text: This is not a residential rehab or a detox. There are no beds, and the clinic does not manage withdrawal. People who need a live-in addiction program should ask about other options on the discovery call. The clinic also does not offer MDMA or psilocybin therapy, which remain controlled in Canada.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Field Trip Health Montreal

faqs.question: Is Field Trip Health Montreal a residential rehab?

answer_blocks.text: No. It is a weekday outpatient clinic on Laurier Ouest, and you leave after every appointment. It has no beds and does not offer detox or withdrawal management. If you need live-in addiction treatment, ask the team on the discovery call or compare residential centres in Montreal and the rest of Quebec.

If you need live-in addiction treatment, ask the team on the discovery call or compare residential centres in Montreal and the rest of Quebec.

answer_blocks.text: The clinic's 2026 Montreal guide lists three programs: Explore, with one dosing session, at $1,430; the KAP Program, with six, at $6,675; and the Plus Program, with nine, at $8,886. The medical consultation that comes first is $250. A deposit of at least 50% secures your schedule, and prices can change, so confirm them on the free discovery call.

faqs.question: Does RAMQ or insurance cover it?

answer_blocks.text: RAMQ does not cover the consultation, the medicine or the medical part of care. Many clients claim the therapy portion through psychotherapy benefits, and the clinic's guide estimates $3,307.50 of the 6-session program could qualify. Nursing benefits on some extended health plans may also help, receipts list therapy and nursing separately, and financing is available. NIHB does not cover ketamine therapy.

faqs.question: Can I get care in French?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. The clinic says its Montreal staff speak both English and French, and its therapists work in both languages. Say which you prefer when you book.

faqs.question: How long is each session and the full program?

answer_blocks.text: A dosing session at the Montreal clinic takes about 2 hours and 15 minutes, including preparation, the medicine and time with your therapist afterwards. Most people do 6 or 9 sessions, each followed by integration, and then meet the team to decide whether ongoing or maintenance care makes sense.

faqs.question: Who is eligible, and do I need a referral?

answer_blocks.text: A nurse practitioner decides eligibility at the medical consultation. The clinic says the treatment may not suit people who are pregnant, allergic to ketamine, have a history of schizophrenia or psychosis, uncontrolled high blood pressure or a severe recent head injury. You can book the discovery call yourself, and doctors and nurse practitioners can also send a referral.

answer_blocks.text: The clinic lists addiction, alcohol use and stimulant use among the concerns it works with, and some clients use ketamine-assisted therapy as part of ongoing care for substance use. It is an outpatient therapy, not a detox or a structured rehab program, so people in active withdrawal or needing daily support will usually need another service first.

faqs.question: Where is the clinic and how do I get there?

answer_blocks.text: The clinic is at 397 Avenue Laurier Ouest, Montréal (H2V 2K3), up the staircase to the right of the Mikado restaurant, last door on the right. Mont-Royal metro is about a 10-minute walk, and the Avenue du Parc and Saint-Joseph bus lines stop nearby. The clinic is not wheelchair accessible because of the stairs, though service animals are welcome.

faqs.question: Can I drive home after a session?

answer_blocks.text: No. Ketamine can leave you drowsy and affect coordination, so the clinic asks you to arrange a ride, a taxi or a rideshare. On other visits there is paid parking at 4251 Rue Saint-Urbain and limited street parking nearby.

faqs.question: Can I keep taking my medication?

answer_blocks.text: Often, yes. Many clients stay on their current medications, and the medical team reviews your list during the consultation to check for anything that needs changing. Do not stop a medication on your own.

faqs.question: Who runs Field Trip Health Montreal?

answer_blocks.text: The clinic is one of eight in-person clinics run as Field Trip Health Canada, alongside Toronto, Ottawa, Vancouver and four other Ontario cities. After the original Field Trip company restructured in 2023, its Canadian clinics continued under separate Canadian ownership. Book through fieldtriphealth.ca.
